notes: MP cited alleged verbal PDS (not IPSA) advice; CO obtained PDS records showing no such query and a Nov 2024 notice (paras 15-16, 28-30); para 33 says no new MP information. IPSA no longer funds IT (17-18, 29). Peripherals resubmittable.

guidance_change_note: No recommendation; notes 18th edition had independently lifted the newsletter ban (paras 21, 39(i)), coded here as VERSION_TIMING.
notes: IPSA's refusal found correct (paras 33-35) but altered to 50% funding on mitigation, few party-political words, and newsletter ban since lifted; MP did not herself ask for an exception. Bright-line NO: party-political/self-promotional tests need content judgment. Non-precedent at para 48.

general_reading: Festive hospitality guidance covers modest refreshments at a work gathering, not staff meals out; a cost failing any one fundamental principle is not claimable (paras 19, 33, 37).
guidance_change_note: IPSA conceded the festive guidance was unclear and said it would update it to exclude team meals out (para 19).
notes: MP relied on published festive FAQ, not staff advice (para 30). Officer found meal separate from away day with no parliamentary purpose (paras 32, 36); info on review not materially new (para 24). Tip barred by explicit rule.

Retrospective request for storage costs after approved period ended March 2024. MP believed costs pre-authorised from earlier approvals and office manager's IPSA contact; Officer found communications clear (paras 28, 31-33). No new information (para 36). Contingency decision discretionary, not bright-line.

general_reading: 'Exceptional' read as unusual/not typical; choosing rent that absorbs the whole accommodation budget, or facing higher energy prices, is not exceptional (para 24a).
notes: Panel refusal upheld, yet Officer allowed a claim up to the unused 2022/23 accommodation budget (GBP 346.85 per para 15) after new information and bill analysis (paras 21, 25); CEO agreed. Not bright-line: discretionary exceptional-circumstances test.

Numeric budget cap; CO says IPSA's repayment demand was correct on information then held (para 31). New facts (ministerial role, consultant moved to payroll) and two-year delay led to para 10.19 discretion (paras 32-40). Precedent disclaimed (paras 38-39).

Contingency bid for utilities overspend refused for lack of exceptionality; CO's own research found large energy rises began April 2022 and affected all MPs (para 28); overspend cannot roll forward (para 30). Footnote cites 11th edition. Exceptionality needs judgment.

guidance_change_note: Only recommendation is MP-specific support or training on the expenses system; no change to rules or guidance proposed (Recommendation).
notes: Officer says IPSA's rejection and internal review were correct under Annex C deadlines (paras 29, 34) yet directs discretion: Covid, new staff, IPSA delays, receipts later found; IPSA director agreed (para 38). Bright-line YES: missed evidence time limit.

Panel credited 721.52 of 1,289.17 for system-caused misapportionment; Officer confirmed 567.65 repayable since double rent arose from MP's personal choice to move (para 22). Account manager backed the application; not coded as past practice. Footnote cites 12th edition.

Summary only; no formal determination (para 1). Claim refused for missing receipt; Officer obtained card statement entry and phone bill, after which IPSA itself allowed the cost (para 4). Substantively the refusal was reversed. Amount not stated. Receipt rule categorical.

Officer found no grounds to alter but sent it back for the panel to weigh discretion (paras 39-40); IPSA then let the overspend carry into 2021/22 (Jan 2022 update). Not bright-line: contingency discretion. Year-end guidance differed from prior year.

Value-for-money refusal; disability assistance is case-by-case, so judgment needed. CO met MP, consulted assessor and supplier (paras 13, 24-26); held IPSA should contribute to one constituency-use cane; GBP300 agreed (paras 27-31). Former-CEO assurance discounted (para 21).

general_reading: Para 4.4 sets out the only associated accommodation costs claimable; household items fall outside it and are not linked to parliamentary functions, so 10.19 discretion is unavailable (paras 21-22).
notes: New MP bought bedding, towels, electricals on payment card, believing start-up costs allowed after IPSA induction meetings; colleagues corroborated (paras 10-13). CO accepted good faith but upheld refusal (21-23). Categorical 4.4 list decides item type.

guidance_change_note: Officer suggests next Scheme edition explain pro-rating; IPSA CEO accepted the recommendation and assured it will be addressed (para 41, Recommendation 1).
notes: Overspend arose because budget was pro-rated to move-out date, before election was called; two of three para 10.10 factors unmet (paras 39-40). Bright-line NO: overspend is arithmetic, but the reviewed panel decision applies discretionary exceptional-circumstances criteria.

Clean and signage (504) allowed: circumstances exceptional, staff acted in good faith, unrecorded IPSA advice credited (paras 31-32). Equipment refusal upheld, IPSA urged to consider reduction (paras 33, 40). Unclear if office manager's account reached panel.

Labelled provisional. Two claims (90 late electrician invoice; 40 BT bill lacking invoice) inside a 2,940.01 overspend. MP's account-manager advice claim disputed by IPSA (para 22). Officer urged lenient debt recovery (para 30). Panel test discretionary; reasons largely rule-based.

general_reading: Employment contract is between MP and staff, so the MP must ensure a signed IPSA-model contract is lodged; failure is not IPSA's responsibility (paras 34-35, 42, 49).
guidance_change_note: Officer recommends IPSA personally contact staff still on Commons contracts and log it; CEO accepted and undertook to act (para 44, Recommendation 1).
notes: Not bright-line: contingency application needing discretionary judgment, though contract type was a categorical fact. Edition from footnote; all editions since 2010 consulted. COMMITTED reflects an accepted process recommendation, not a rule change. Scope coding is a judgment call.

general_reading: Cleaning exclusion read as covering routine cleaning during occupation; an end-of-tenancy deep clean required by an IPSA-approved lease is distinct and may count as a service charge (paras 24-27).
guidance_change_note: CO suggests next Scheme edition distinguish general from end-of-tenancy cleaning and clarify lease 'approval' versus registration (Review Recommendation; Appendix One).
notes: Tension: para 24 states a reading of the cleaning exclusion, yet Appendix One disclaims precedent. Panel applied categorical exclusion; CO reinterpreted, so judgment needed. Comparator MPs were paid; IPSA says in error (para 28, fn 4). 11th/12th editions also mentioned.

general_reading: Para 4.5 cleaning exclusion covers cleaning during occupation, not a lease-required end-of-tenancy deep clean, which can count as a service charge where IPSA approved the lease (paras 24-27, 29).
guidance_change_note: Recommends next Scheme edition clarify lease 'approval' (4.21) and claimable service charges; IPSA agreed to consider this (para 34, Recommendation, App. 1).
notes: Contingency panel refused clean/making-good as personal cost; CO allowed 715.20 citing IPSA lease approval and ambiguous wording, disclaiming precedent (para 34, App. 1). Figures inconsistent (710.40/715.40/715.20); 85.48 rent dropped by MP. 11th edition cited in footnote.

guidance_change_note: Review Comment says confusion over when depreciation calculations are considered needs to be addressed (after para 44).
notes: Panel right to refuse full cost (poor value for money); Officer grants 60 pounds for six weeks' work use, noting IPSA email effectively permitted purchase; figure uses IPSA depreciation data obtained in review. Contingency criteria discretionary; para 8.6 bar categorical.

Invoice went to deactivated parliamentary email; MP unaware until re-election (paras 28, 35). IPSA objected in App. 2; Officer replied no floodgates, each case on its facts. Panel decision was discretionary, though 90-day limit itself is bright-line.

general_reading: 'Exceptional circumstances' under the Scheme must arise from the MP's parliamentary role, not personal circumstances; discretion outside the Scheme is likewise tied to the parliamentary role (paras 27, 52-53, 60).
notes: Former MP sought a month's rent plus removals beyond the two-month wind-up. Officer used own research (death notice) on avoidability (para 28). MP said she followed IPSA/lawyer advice (para 43); not expressly addressed, so borderline. Discretionary tests need judgment.

expense_category: legal fees vacant possession own property
general_reading: 'Exceptional' for contingency purposes means circumstances arising from the parliamentary role, not personal ones; para 4.14 legal costs cover only moves while in office (Considerations paras 15, 19).
notes: Not bright-line: panel decision turned on discretionary 'exceptional circumstances' test, though ineligibility of the fees themselves was categorical. Claim first paid then clawed back; MP cited wind-up meeting advice. Paragraph numbering restarts mid-document.

guidance_change_note: CO asks IPSA to consider amending the Scheme to cover short-term temporary lets, especially for newly elected MPs (Review Recommendation); IPSA accepted (para 48).
notes: Contingency Panel refused: unsigned tenancy, no registration, 90-day limit. CO found unanswered advice request, panel confused two tenancy emails, Scheme gap for short lets (paras 41-46). Holiday-let nature clarified on review (para 41); unrecorded phone advice claimed (para 40).

general_reading: Volunteers' food/drink expenses under para 7.24 are payable only when linked to travel for a volunteering-related purpose; lunches bought while working from home are ineligible (paras 21.12-21.17, 22.2).
guidance_change_note: IPSA should reword the Scheme on volunteers' incidental expenses to state the travel link, and possibly amend the model volunteer form (21.6, 22.4, Recommendation).
notes: CO agreed with IPSA's reading while calling the wording ambiguous (21.6, 22.3-22.4); said Scheme gives no discretion here (21.19-21.24). MP's prior-payments inconsistency argument (17.2; App. 2) not expressly answered. Text lacked the travel condition, so interpretation needed.

general_reading: 'Unavoidable' in para 6.19 is undefined, so takes its ordinary meaning of not able to be prevented; inability to secure a two-month break clause can qualify (para 46).
guidance_change_note: Recommends personal contact with MPs affected by Scheme amendments, and further guidance clarifying 'unavoidable' with evidence expectations (Review Recommendations 1-2).
notes: Written 2016 assurance from IPSA senior manager, rule tightened after lease signed, and weak communication led Officer to overturn contingency panel. Bright-line NO: two-month limit numeric but 'unavoidable' exception needs judgment; panel itself wavered. Para 54 later restates sums owed.

general_reading: Undefined term 'unavoidable' in para 6.19 takes its ordinary meaning, not able to be prevented; a documented landlord refusal to add a two-month break clause meets it (para 47).
guidance_change_note: No new recommendations beyond those made in an earlier review on the same subject (para 58); paras 43-45 criticise IPSA's communication.
notes: Editions 4th, 7th and 9th used; 11th current. Lease signed 2015 under advisory guidance after IPSA reassurance (para 39); 2017 rule added 'unavoidable' test. Unclear whether landlord letter was before the panel.

general_reading: Scheme wording supports allocating expenses to the budget year in which the transaction occurred, not the year the cost relates to, absent a timely year-end form (paras 23-25, 38).
guidance_change_note: Officer suggested IPSA consider clearer guidance on payment-card and year-end processes and better MP access to payment information (paras 35, 39-40).
notes: Full-year council tax (1627.96) paid by IPSA card 27 Mar 2017; no year-end form by 13 Apr, so charged to 2016-17, creating overspend. Edition question held immaterial (para 20). MP cited IPSA email and prior-year card practice. Date/budget rules numeric.

general_reading: Claims are judged solely within the Scheme; informal staff advice or apparent prior approval creates no legitimate expectation; the cleaning exclusion is unequivocal (paras 13, 17).
guidance_change_note: Suggests IPSA restate that no pre-advice or prior approval exists and clarify end-of-lease cleaning clauses (paras 18-19).
notes: Bright-line: para 4.5a categorically excludes cleaning and the claim was described as cleaning, though a validator first allowed it after reading the lease. MP relied on wind-up meeting advice; rejected.

guidance_change_note: CO recommends reminding IPSA staff to record all claim communications in CRM; supports record-keeping help for MP's office (Review Recommendations 1-2; IPSA accepted, para 52).
notes: Mixed: flight invoices missed 30-day evidence deadline, mechanical, upheld (paras 39, 47-48). Subsistence form mis-completed and IPSA wrongly held back hotel invoice; CO allowed GBP300 on balance using proxy's 7 March note (paras 49-51).

general_reading: Scheme lets IPSA allocate a cost to the budget year in which the transaction took place, not the year the goods or services relate to (para 20; see also 32-34).
guidance_change_note: Suggests IPSA consider clearer payment-card/direct-payment and year-end procedures, and better MP access to payment information (paras 30, 35-36).
notes: Council tax part (1035.00) confirmed; cartridges part (669.74) allowed because refusing discretion was unreasonable given supplier's written assurance on charge date, supplied after initial refusal (paras 27, 37-39). Edition question raised but immaterial (16-17). Original allocation was date-based.

general_reading: A communication to many constituents on several diverse issues is a newsletter whether paper or electronic; the exclusion extends to associated production and distribution costs (paras 27-28, 30).
notes: Paid via streamlined validation, rejected after FOI-prompted re-scrutiny. MP argued cost was software and rule targets glossy print. Staff email advice held to have no bearing (para 26). Bright-line YES: evidence filed with claim called it a newsletter.

general_reading: Office costs cover only renting, equipping and running an office; paying record fees for constituents is a gift to them and not claimable, whether or not other funding exists (paras 36-39).
notes: Claims auto-paid then rejected on post-payment scrutiny. 25 earlier and 3 later similar claims paid; Officer applied Scheme para 2.3 so past allowance had no bearing (para 34). Scheme silent on such costs; original call needed parliamentary-purpose judgment.

general_reading: No distinction can be drawn between bags for carrying electronic documents and briefcases for paper; if laptop bags are allowable, briefcases must be too (para 42).
guidance_change_note: Officer asked IPSA to look at future laptop-bag and briefcase claims so validators apply rules uniformly (para 43); IPSA will consider implications (App. A).
notes: Officer found arguments near evenly balanced; decisive factor was his own research showing 19 laptop-bag claims paid in 2015-16 (paras 32-34, 41-42); OTHER = consistency of treatment. MP did not cite past payments. Reasonableness and 'other citizens' tests need judgment.

general_reading: Where the Scheme gives MPs discretion, promoting local business counts as parliamentary; IPSA should not second-guess reasonable methods; mentioning prizes does not bar a leaflet (paras 23, 25).
guidance_change_note: Officer invites IPSA to weigh this case in its ongoing Scheme review of 'parliamentary functions' and MP discretion (para 33).
notes: Not bright-line: needed judgment on whether leaflet served parliamentary functions under 6.1/6.5. Paid, then rejected post-payment. Later-facts true because comparator claims by other MPs were gathered at review (para 20). Prior-year approval: not binding but weakened IPSA's case (paras 14-15).

Year-end 60-day deadline missed by 15 days; login-token problems, workload and proxy's misunderstanding treated as mitigation only (paras 34, 44-47). IPSA letter mentions IT work with Commons and past flexibility for genuine cases (Annex E); not a rules change.

general_reading: Listing every ward councillor makes their shared party irrelevant; Scheme has no font/colour rules so these cannot decide payment; councillor content is non-parliamentary, so cost is apportioned (paras 24-25, 29-32).
notes: Claim refused as political; CO allowed half, treating councillor portion as non-parliamentary (paras 32-34). Pre-claim phone/email advice held outside review scope (para 29a). Political-vs-parliamentary classification and the 50/50 split needed judgment.

Paid, then recovered after post-payment check. MP said mailings were meeting invitations; Officer found one side plainly a newsletter (paras 20-25). Bright-line YES: categorical exclusion and invoice itself said newsletter leaflets. Unclear when IPSA first saw the mailings.

Amount is sum of para 30 portions (525 disallowed as shadow ministerial, 175 allowed). Officer used own internet research and briefing supplied on review (paras 20-23). Staff assurances uncontested but held unable to influence outcome (para 25).

general_reading: Which Scheme edition governs is fixed by the date the cost was incurred, not the payment date, and reviews rest on the Scheme itself rather than IPSA guidance (paras 33-34).
notes: IPSA used card payment date (June 2015) to apply the 7th edition hospitality ban; Officer used supply date (Feb 2015) under the 6th. Both dates were on the submitted invoice; rule categorical once governing date fixed. Guidance omitted ban.

expense_category: late year-end utilities and office bills
general_reading: A s6A review tests only whether IPSA applied the Scheme and its policies correctly; mitigating circumstances such as technical problems or the election fall outside it (para 29).
notes: Bright-line: expense dates versus the 30 May year-end cut-off settle it (paras 18, 25, 30). Amount summed from five Annex A lines; no total stated. Scope coding is a judgment call (remit statement, not a Scheme term).

Fixed nightly hotel caps applied to invoice amounts (paras 28, 30-31). CO says above-cap discretion needs contemporaneous contact with IPSA showing search efforts; none recorded (paras 26, 29). Late card reconciliation mentioned but not the refusal ground.

Former MP relied on IPSA's Jan 2015 meeting/statement and IPSA's admitted errors (paras 23-26); CO rechecked the figures and held public money must be repaid regardless (paras 27-29). Overspend is arithmetic against a fixed budget.

general_reading: The Scheme prevails over conflicting IPSA guidance; staff travel between a staff member's home office and Westminster is not claimable under the 4th or 5th editions (paras 33-36).
guidance_change_note: Criticises unclear guidance and lack of written no-show policy (paras 30, 36, 69, 73) without recommending change; para 44 invitation concerns this debt only.
notes: Two parts: staff travel/hotel claims (paid, later clawed back) confirmed not allowable; card debt mostly confirmed, no-show fees allowed, two items conceded mid-review. Mixed: caps and journey types categorical, but hotel 'unreasonable to return' and no-show tests need judgment.

general_reading: Para 9.2.a needs two stages: identify each journey (single only if essentially uninterrupted; purpose can make a stop its own destination), then test parliamentary necessity; dual purpose generally disqualifies (paras 42-46).
guidance_change_note: Fifth edition (from April 2013) lets MPs claim diverted constituency-London journeys, capped at the direct standard open fare (paras 25-27).
notes: Rehearing on agreed facts. Total GBP 296.35; second leg (272.45) conceded by Compliance Officer after appeal lodged; first leg (23.90) held properly refused. Tribunal called both readings arguable (para 3), so original refusal needed judgment.

guidance_change_note: Officer said IPSA should consider the MP's arguments at its next Scheme review and forwarded her letter (para 8).
notes: MP did not deny the item was a newsletter; she attacked the exclusion as irrational and biased against print (coded OTHER). Officer found a 12.06 VAT under-refusal but waived recovery. Bright-line: categorical newsletter exclusion in guidance to 10.4(e).
